paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz M282 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to — the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required — submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead — strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most M282 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting — sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call — particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild — a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle — restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six M282-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-Benz M282 engine?
faqLeft.a: The M282 is a 1.3-litre turbocharged inline-four petrol engine, developed in partnership with the Renault-Nissan Alliance, in production since 2018.

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes-Benz models use the M282?
faqLeft.a: A-Class, CLA, GLA-Class and Citan — see the full applications table above for exact variants and years.

faqLeft.q: Does the M282 differ between Mercedes-Benz models?
faqLeft.a: Yes. The specific ancillaries and mounting differ by application, even though the base engine code is the same. We match by registration/VIN before confirming any rebuild or replacement.

faqLeft.q: Is an M282 from one Mercedes-Benz model compatible with another?
faqLeft.a: Not automatically. An M282 from an A-Class isn't a drop-in match for an M282 from a Citan — ancillaries and mounting differ. We always confirm compatibility by registration/VIN.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-Benz M282 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £2,200, regardless of which model it's fitted to. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on M282 rebuilds across every model it's fitted to, replacing worn components as standard.

faqLeft.q: Do you work on M282 mild-hybrid applications?
faqLeft.a: Yes. M282 MHEV applications are within our workshop capability, with the relevant 48V ancillaries accounted for once your exact model is confirmed.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M282 from an A-Class?
faqRight.a: Yes. The M282 in the A-Class is one of the most common applications we see, across both the A 180 and A 200.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M282 from a Citan?
faqRight.a: Yes. The M282 in the Citan is one of the applications we work on, for the 112 and 113 petrol variants.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-Benz M282 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes-Benz if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an M282 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most M282 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history — a particular concern given the engine's application across different Mercedes-Benz models — and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
